claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain than commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater toughness than commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
The proposed improvements in plastic strain and toughness are governed by the alloy's heterogeneous microstructure.
Processed WTaTiVZr develops a multiphase microstructure containing fine precipitates.
Conventional pure tungsten has a comparatively homogeneous microstructure.
The precipitates and phase boundaries in WTaTiVZr remain stable during the proposed high-temperature exposure.
Fine precipitates and phase boundaries act as internal barriers to deformation.
Fine precipitates and phase boundaries assist activation of additional slip systems.
The proposed microstructural features promote dynamic strain aging.
Additional slip activity and dynamic strain aging produce more uniformly distributed plastic deformation.
More uniformly distributed plastic deformation enhances toughness and delays fracture.
Under identical high-temperature plasma-facing conditions, WTaTiVZr will retain a fine precipitate structure and exhibit distributed deformation.
Under the same conditions, pure tungsten will exhibit localized deformation.
Under the same conditions, pure tungsten will fail in a brittle manner.
The proposed mechanism is predominantly valid from approximately 1000 to 1500 degrees Celsius when irradiation and thermal cycling are present.
The mechanism may not apply at lower temperatures or under substantially different loading conditions.
The relative plastic strain and toughness can be tested by exposing WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten to nominally identical high-temperature tensile or creep conditions.
The hypothesis would be falsified if WTaTiVZr did not show significantly higher plastic strain and toughness than pure tungsten under identical conditions.
The hypothesis would be falsified if the predicted fine precipitates and associated dynamic strain processes were not detected.
